chapter: Union, New Orleans and King Oliver
title: The Oliver band bus wreck and Ross McConnell's money
summary: Reason tells how Oliver's bus went off a West Virginia mountain, Oliver's back was hurt, and the band was stranded.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: So you were quite young. Oh, yeah. I see. And, uh, when you were with King Oliver, how did you travel? At that time, you said the bus burned up, they got a new bus?

He got another bus through this guy, Ross McConnell. Mm-hmm. He got the bus, that's how he had his, his, uh, finger down, uh, uh, uh, King Oliver's throat. Because he had all that. And he borrowed money. Borrowed money from the, uh, the club owners.

And, uh, they, uh, when, band get there, and after we play, find out there's nothing coming, because Ross is back in, you know, Chicago somewhere. And, uh, he borrowed the money and moved no money from, for King. And we had to wait until Ross sent his money to go to the next town, to the next dance. Then there's something happened to the bus. Then we were in, um, Hunter from West Virginia. It went, uh, and the bus got really, really bad. It couldn't make mountains anymore. Mm-hmm. And, um, oh, just before then, we were going on our way, going to Bluefield. And, uh, coming to it, we had, uh, a fellow from Huntington was driving for us named Hale. I forget the young boy in there. And, uh, there's Hale, I forget his last name. But he was driving the bus, and as he was coming out of the, coming down to the mountain, uh, he took the, the bus out of gear. Mm-hmm. He started neutral, and he couldn't get it back in. Instead of doing this while he's going up the hill, when he got to the top of the hill, and, uh, he waited until he started back down, because he needed the brakes and the, uh, the, the, the transmission to, uh, stop the bus, to slow it down. Mm-hmm. And that bus got away from him, and it got down so that the left front wheel went off the side of the mountain, just like this. And I looked down. I was sitting on that side.

I looked down, and I saw it was about two city blocks down below us, the railroad track, Mm-hmm. Way down there. And King Alva was sitting. He always sat on the front, right seat. Mm-hmm. And when that bus did that, he got his back hurt. And I don't think he ever got better from that. Yeah. And three or four was in the band, because everybody wanted to get out of, try to jump out of the bus, you know. Mm-hmm. And I was sitting, I had, um, something with my, uh, my foot, like, uh, it was like, like, uh, something like arthritis, something on that order. But I couldn't do much getting around. And I couldn't get out, because I was sitting right back of here. And I used to sit back of him all the time to keep him from going to sleep, you know. And, uh, if he'd get tired, then I'd get him at the wheel and drive. But I could drive all night after we'd get off from work. And I'd drive some time all night to keep him from going to sleep. Mm-hmm. Because I knew he was going to go to sleep, but he wouldn't stay up all night, galley hooking around, you know. He was crazy about those little gals. And you find one, he'd almost die by, he's one of these guys falling in love.

And, uh, so when we got that bus back to Huntington, we stayed there about two months without any work at all. And when we got ready to, he did book us back, uh, to work. Ross did book us back to work. And then the people, uh, King Oliver was ready from, was my lady's name was Mrs. Wisnet. W-I-Z-E-N-T. Mm-hmm. And she had a call that was just about a year or two old. And her husband let Mrs. Wisnet go with us to collect so much money per day. And she would work the doors for King because they both were crazy about King. See, King was pretty fast talking.

He knew, he knew how to, he could, he could, he could twist it around his little finger in a minute, you know. And, uh, he kept folks laughing all the time. And, uh, we went down, took that car and two other cars. One belonged to Buck, uh, another bus driver, what we had, got with us. So he had, uh, a Ford automobile, two seats. And Mrs. Wisnet drove her car and we had another car, I think we read it. And, uh, that was almost getting to the winding up of King Oliver before Paul left. Mm-hmm. And, uh, he never did get, get over that, that, that wreck. Never did get over that wreck. Like every time something would just get up to where it would look like we're gonna pull out, something else would happen. If it wasn't automobile flat tires or, or get into the mountains and, uh, uh, rear axle would go out or transmission would go out. It just seemed like from one bad degree to another. And that's what caused most of the, uh, older musicians who had been there, who really knew the band, who had one fella, um, live in Washington, D.C. He was the road manager. And I don't know his name, good as a book, I don't remember his name. But those fellas quit, had to quit, go back on, because there was nothing else.
